title: Training Controllable World Models via Action Influence Maximization
title_zh: 【第一行翻译】通过行动影响力最大化训练可控世界模型

paragraphs.en: 本文提出行动影响力最大化算法AIM，通过主动收集数据提升世界模型的行动可控性，大幅降低所需数据量。 Action-conditioned video generative models trained on successful, goal-directed demonstrations tend to ignore the commanded action, rendering a plausible expert-like future regardless of what is asked of them. We trace this failure to training data that lack sufficient action influence. We analyze this metric and prove that it upper bounds the action influence that any model trained on that data can express. Expert demonstrations, whose narrow action distributions let next states be predicted without attending to the action, set a low ceiling that no amount of model capacity alone can raise. Raising it requires collecting different data. We introduce Action Influence Maximization (AIM), an algorithm for actively collecting training data for improving dataset action influence. We compare the performance and data-efficiency of AIM against exploration heuristics and intrinsic-motivation methods on simulated navigation and manipulation tasks. In pixel-based manipulation, AIM is the only method that consistently improves controllability: 500 actively collected episodes added to 3k demonstrations match a world model trained on 300k expert episodes on end-effector controllability, an $85\times$ reduction in data.
paragraphs.zh: 本文提出行动影响力最大化算法AIM，通过主动收集数据提升世界模型的行动可控性，大幅降低所需数据量。基于成功的目标导向演示训练的动作条件视频生成模型往往会忽略指令动作，无论要求它做什么，都生成一个看似合理的类专家未来。 我们将这一失败归因于训练数据缺乏足够的动作影响力。 我们对该度量进行分析，并证明它为任何在该数据上训练的模型所能表达的动作影响力提供了上界。 专家演示的动作分布狭窄，使得模型无需关注动作即可预测下一状态，其设定了一个低上限，仅靠增加模型容量无法突破。 要提高这一上限，需要收集不同的数据。 我们提出行动影响力最大化（AIM），一种通过主动收集训练数据来提升数据集动作影响力的算法。 我们在仿真导航与操作任务上，将AIM的性能与数据效率同探索启发式方法和内在动机方法进行比较。 在基于像素的操作任务中，AIM是唯一能持续提升可控性的方法：在3千条演示基础上添加500条主动收集的片段，其末端执行器可控性可与基于30万条专家片段训练的世界模型相匹配，数据量减少了$85\times$倍。
